chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The guest, when he steals, his hand is not cut, and if the guest invites a guest and he steals, the hand of the guest of the guest is cut.

key_terms.ضَيْفُ الضَّيْفِ: The guest of the guest (secondary visitor)
key_terms.قُطِعَ: It was cut (referring to the hand)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in theft punishment between a primary guest and a secondary guest in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential distinction between a primary guest (who retains the protection of their host's hospitality) and a secondary guest (who is considered a stranger to the host and thus liable for standard theft penalties). It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the social contract of *diyafah* (hospitality) as a mitigating factor in criminal law, reflecting the nuanced application of *hudud* punishments in early Islamic society.
